reason: Python's argparse took prog from the invoked script (tools/<tool>.py); the Go binaries are run as their installed command (tools/install.sh), so usage and help name that command, not a retired .py script. The Go --dangling help states what the JSON `dangling` field means (CHECK7) and that it is not an unresolved source.

usage: bognav [bog] links [-h] [--json] [--csv] [--limit N] [--to TO] [--from FROM_] [--slot SLOT]
                          [--slot-any] [--dangling] [--src SRC]

options:
  -h, --help     show this help message and exit
  --json         machine JSON output
  --csv          CSV output (header + rows)
  --limit, -n N  print at most N rows (default: all); the cut is reported
  --to TO        target path/component
  --from FROM_   source path/component
  --slot SLOT    exact slot name on the --from source end / the --to target end (either end when
                 neither is given)
  --slot-any     --slot matches either end regardless of --from/--to (pre-2026-09-06 behaviour)
  --dangling     only links whose targetSlotName no @NiagaraProperty under --src declares (CHECK7;
                 the JSON "dangling" field; not an unresolved source, see src_resolved)
  --src SRC      module src root: resolve --dangling (CHECK7)
